questions.question: How is per capita income calculated?
questions.solution: Per capita income, also called income per person is the mean income of the people in a country or an economic unit. It is calculated by dividing the GDP or gross national income by the population.

questions.question: Which of the following is/are required to get more income by the people?
questions.solution: All of the above things are required to get more income.

questions.question: Under which article the President can declare National Emergency in India?
questions.solution: Under the Article 352 of the Indian Constitution, the President can declare a National Emergency on the basis of a written request by the Prime Minister and the Cabinet. It is declared on three grounds which include external aggression, war, and armed rebellion.

questions.question: Which Article of Indian Constitution deals with ‘Rights to Education'?
questions.solution: Article 21a of the Indian Constitution deals with the Right to Education. The Constitution (Eighty-sixth Amendment) Act, 2002 inserted Article 21-A in the Constitution of India to provide free and compulsory education of all children in the age group of six to fourteen years as a Fundamental Right.

questions.question: Where did Gautama Buddha teach for the first time?
questions.solution: The Deer Park in Sarnath was the place where Gautama Buddha first taught the dharma after attaining enlightenment, in which he spoke about the 4 noble truths and teachings associated with it. Sarnath is also one of the 4 pilgrimage places mentioned by Buddha himself to where his devout followers visit.

questions.question: Who was the last of the powerful Mughal rulers?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Aurangzeb**__, the son of Emperor Shah Jahan, was the sixth and the last true powerful Mughal ruler.
 
• The Mughal Empire during his reign temporarily reached its great extent.
 
• He was a notable expansionist and reigned for 49 years from 1658 until his death in 1707.

questions.question: What is a strait?

options.text: A narrow strip of land joining two landmasses
A narrow strip of land joining two water bodies
A narrow passage of water connecting two large water bodies
A narrow passage of water connecting two landmasses

questions.solution: A strait is a narrow, naturally formed waterway or passage which connects two large water bodies. It is a channel of water that lies between two land masses.

questions.question: Which is the largest ocean of the world?
questions.solution: The Pacific Ocean is the deepest and the largest of all the world ocean basins. It contains more than half of the free water on the Earth and covers 59 million square miles approximately. The Pacific basin can fit in all of the world’s continents, such is its hugeness.

questions.question: What is the surroundings in which organisms live called?
questions.solution: The surroundings in which organisms live is called a habitat. A habitat is characterized by both biological and physical features. A habitat for a species is that place where it can find food, shelter, mates for reproduction, and protection.

questions.question: Which of the following wavelength of light is absorbed the most for photosynthesis?
questions.solution: Blue light is absorbed by the carotenoids, which further pass the energy to the chlorophyll. Red light is known to be the most effective wavelength of light in photosynthesis since both the photosystems absorb light of the wavelength in the red region, that is, in 680 and 700 nm respectively.

questions.question: Which device is used to test whether an object is carrying charge or not?
questions.solution:
__Explanation:__

There are two types of charges found in nature -

 
• Positive charge
 
• Negative charge

 

Properties of charges:

 
• Like charges (same charges) repel each other.
 
• Unlike charges (different charges) attract each other.

 

When two objects are rubbed against each other, they develop charges.

Electroscope: An electroscope is a device which is used to test whether an object is carrying a charge or not.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/303f93280fa8a8b4bea25c6cdd789d50f15ae9e3ba13e2e3b002c0fdec0487e8.png] 

The **aluminium foil strips receive the same charge** from the charged refill through the paper clip (remember that metals are good conductors of electricity).

The strips carrying similar charges repel each other and they become wide open. 

Whereas,

 
• A **thermometer** is a device that **measures temperature** gradient or temperature.
 
• A **stethoscope** is a medical device used by the doctors for listening to the internal sounds of a human body or an animal.
 
• An **odometer **is an instrument which is used to measure the distance travelled by a vehicle.

 

Hence, **Electroscope is correct option.**

questions.question: If the reflecting surface of a spherical mirror curves outwards, then it is a ________ mirror.
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Convex mirrors**__ are those spherical mirrors which have **__reflective surfaces that curve outwards__**.
 
• Concave mirrors are those spherical mirrors which are curved inward in the middle.
 
• A plane mirror has a flat reflective surface.
 
• Plano-convex lenses are optical lenses which have a positive focal length.

questions.question: Which of the following options is **NOT** correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 1024 bytes are there in a kilobyte.
 
• 1KB= 1024 byte.
 
• 1 Byte = 8 bit.
 
• 1KB = 1024*8 bits.
 
• **1KB = 8192 bits.**
 
• 1MB = 1024 KB
 
• 1GB = 1024MB

So, **1KB** is **not equal** to **8000 bits**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kilobyte :**

 
 
• **The kilobyte is a multiple-unit byte for digital information.**
 
• The International System of Units (SI) defines the prefix kilo as 1000); per this definition, one kilobyte is 1000 bytes.
 
• The internationally recommended unit symbol for the kilobyte is kB.
 
 
 
• **Bit :** 
 
 
• A bit is a basic unit of information in **information theory, computing, and digital communications.**
 
• The name is a portmanteau of binary digits.
 
• **The smallest unit of measurement used for measuring data is a bit.**
 
• A single bit can have a value of either zero(0) or one(1).
 
• It may contain a binary value (such as True/False or On/Off or 1/0) and nothing more.
 
• Therefore, a byte, or eight bits, is used as the fundamental unit of measurement for data storage. 
 
• **Computer storage and memory are often measured in megabytes (MB) and gigabytes (GB).**
 
• A medium-sized novel contains about 1 MB of information. 
 
 
 
• **Calculate kb. to bit :**
 
 
• **1 Kilobyte is equal to 8192 Bit (eight thousand one hundred ninety two-bit)**
 
• 1 Bit is equal to 0.000125 Kilobyte (zero point zero × 3 one hundred and twenty-five kb)
 
 
 
• Byte:
 
 
• A** byte** is a data measurement unit that contains eight bits, or a series of eight zeros and ones. A single **byte** can be used to represent 28 or 256 different values.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• 1 KB or 1 Kilobyte is equal to 8192 bits.
 
• 1 gigabyte is equal to 1024 megabytes.
 
• 1 Kilobyte=1024 byte.
 
• 1 Megabyte = 1024 kilobytes

questions.question: Metals generally form ________.
questions.solution:
Metal oxides are basic in nature since they react with dilute acids to form salt and water. When they react with water, they form metal hydroxides which are also alkaline in nature since they release OH- ions in the solution.

The non-metallic oxides form acidic solutions when they react with water and release H+ ions in the solution. Thus, they are acidic in nature.

questions.question: The absolute charge of the electron is ________.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• An electron is a negatively charged particle that has an absolute charge of 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ coulombs. 
 
• The charge of an electron was **first measured by Robert Millikan in his famous oil-drop experiment.** Based on his experiments, the elementary charge (the charge of a single electron or proton) was determined to be approximately** 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.**
 
• Later, more precise measurements using techniques like mass spectrometry refined the value to the currently accepted value of 1.602176634 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.

questions.question: Which one of the following is not among the three R's to save the environment?
questions.solution:
• The three R’s of the environment are Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle.
 
• Reduce- Reducing the amount of waste produced in order to help the environment.
 
• Reuse- Try to use used things again instead of throwing them.
 
• Recycle- Recycle items to make new products out of them.

questions.question: Which among the following scheme aims to provide 24 x 7 uninterrupted electricity supply to each rural household across the country by 2022?

options.text: Unnat Jyoti by Affordable LEDs for All

questions.solution: The Deendayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana is a scheme launched by the government of India which aims to provide 24 x 7 uninterrupted electricity supply to each rural household across the country by 2022. It was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and it aims to strengthen distribution and sub-transmission network to prevent power losses.

questions.question: Who discovered the double helical structure of DNA?
questions.solution: James Watson and Francis Crick discovered the double helical structure of DNA in 1953. This discovery gave rise to the modern molecular biology and marked a milestone in the history of science. The discovery was largely concerned with understanding how genes control the chemical processes within the cells.

questions.question: Who won the Best Supporting Actress award at the 64th National Film Awards?
questions.solution: The 64th National Film Awards was an award ceremony during which the best films of the year 2016 were honoured with National Film Awards presented by the Directorate of Film Festivals. questions.question: Which country has been designated as major defence partner of the US?
questions.solution: India has been designated as major defence partner of the US. It puts India on a par with the closest partners and allies of the US. The agreement was reached between the US Secretary of Defence Ashton Carter and Union Defence Minister Manohar Parrikar in New Delhi.

questions.question: The Agra-Summit was organized with the aim of resolving long-standing issues between India and _________.
questions.solution: The Agra Summit was a historic 2-day summit meeting which took place from 14-16 July 2001 and was organized with the aim of resolving long-standing issues between India and Pakistan. A proposal was made during the meeting to solve issues pertaining to cross-border terrorism and the Kashmir dispute, and to drastically reduce the nuclear arsenals.
